items.snippet: The otherworldly Cinque Torri are a landmark mountaintop rock formation and a key starting point for skiing, hiking and rock climbing.

The relaxed, tradition-rooted El Brite de Larieto and its more experimental Michelin-starred sibling restaurant, SanBrite, both source ingredients from El Brite’s own farm, and offer two very different but essential dining destinations.

Inside the 1804 Hotel de la Poste, the eminently antique Bar del Posta has served luminaries of every era, among them Ernest Hemingway, whose favorite corner bears the author’s inscription.

The Tofane peaks are the town’s backyard mountains and the symbol of Alpine life and snow sports in Cortina.
Corso Italia, running the length of Cortina’s pedestrianized center, is the town’s central artery and the place for both shopping and the evening passeggiata.

items.place: Mario Rimoldi Museum of Modern Art
items.snippet: Three municipal museums – the Mario Rimoldi Museum of Modern Art, the Paleontology Museum and the Ethnographic Museum – offer visitors a cultural and deep-time introduction to Cortina.

One-hour classes at the glass workshop of Claudia Alverà are a hands-on introduction to local craft.
Ice-skate at the rink of Olympians, the Modernist Stadio Olimpico del Ghiaccio.
Stargaze from a pristine mountain plateau at Cortina’s Helmut Ullrich Astronomical Observatory.
Alajmo Cortina is part of the expanding restaurant empire of the Alajmo brothers, Italian fine-dining legends.
Experience technique-forward takes on Alpine eating at 1224, inside the Grand Hotel Savoia.
Ristorante Ra Stua, founded in 1937, serves classic Tyrolean cuisine.
Enjoy an aperitivo and make friends with the regulars at the compact and convivial Enoteca Cortina.
Drink like the locals do at El Becalen, a decades-old, wood-paneled institution.
Take in a supreme view of the Cinque Torri rock stacks over lunch or an après-ski drink at the mountaintop Rifugio Scoiattoli.
Indulge in Cortina’s sweets tradition with Hapsburg-inspired pastries at Pasticceria Alverà.
La Fregola prepares homestyle desserts with recipes passed down by grandmothers.
Dress like a chic mountain denizen with artisan-crafted clothing from Paoletti di Follina 1795.
Ghedina Zuccaro offers classical Alpine styles for men, women and children.
Cozy up your home with handmade housegoods from Magamaison.
Find felted Alpine slippers amid the jumble at Sottosopra.
Outdo the designer-clad ski set with niche-brand sunglasses from Indice.
The densely packed Verocai Antiques has vintage works of art and local craftsmanship.

With the Olympics boosting Cortina’s already considerable clout, investors are converting historic guesthouses into luxury hotels. The symbol of Cortina’s new era is the Hotel Ancora Cortina, a previously faded 200-year-old hotel at the very heart of Cortina, revived by the fashi

Also on Corso Italia, Hotel Cortina has been run by the same local family since opening in 1870, and maintains traditional Tyrolean flower-painted furnishings, plus suites for parents with children and a popular bar (rooms from €330).
Elsewhere in the center, the family-owned Ciasa Lorenzi has recently remodeled, lightheartedly kitschy Alpine rooms (from €220).
